public_rationale: TruthfulQA, introduced in 2021 and revised in May 2022, reported truthful answers on 58% of questions for the best tested model, compared with 94% for humans [e8]. The March 2022 GopherCite study reported no improvement under TruthfulQA's truthfulness measure despite producing answers with supporting evidence [e9]. Neither study isolates the causal contribution of reference, cognitive models or compositionality, so the proposed explanation remains unresolved [e8, e9].
limitations: TruthfulQA's questions target misconceptions; its results do not establish an overall factual-error rate [e8].
The cited results concern answer generation rather than a direct test of classifying supplied statements as true or false [e8, e9].
GopherCite does not separately manipulate the three proposed capabilities or rule out their causal contribution [e9].

our_interpretation: The surrounding introduction makes this a causal claim about reference, cognitive models and compositionality, not merely an observation that models sometimes give false answers.
Distinguishing truth from falsehood means reliably selecting or identifying factually correct statements against plausible false alternatives.
False-answer generation is relevant but does not by itself identify an inability to discriminate truth or its cause.
The causal phrase is not an antecedent of a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evidence shows that deficiencies in the specified capabilities materially impair true-versus-false discrimination in contemporary models, and that targeted interventions improve it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Well-controlled tests rule out a material causal contribution from those deficiencies, or establish an opposite effect, on representative truth-discrimination tasks.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton and Owain Evans
evidence.explanation: TruthfulQA documents false-answer generation in GPT-family and other models on questions designed to elicit misconceptions. It does not manipulate reference, cognitive models or compositionality, so the reported failures do not establish the causal claim.

GopherCite adds retrieved supporting evidence and preference-based training, yet does not improve this truthfulness measure. This cautions against equating source grounding with truth, but does not refute the broader claim involving all three linguistic factors.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled experiments on models available by June 22, 2022, that separately vary the proposed capabilities and measure discrimination between independently verified true and false statements while controlling supervision and training objectives.
